yaml.title: Xavier Gonzalez
yaml.description: Parallelizing Dynamical Systems in Artificial Intelligence

markdown.markdown: ::: {.column-page-inset-left} ![](sequential_vs_parallel.gif){.rounded .intro-pic width=450} I am a final-year PhD student studying Artificial Intelligence at Stanford. My advisor is [Scott Linderman](https://lindermanlab.github.io/). My thesis research focuses on developing and studying methods to **parallelize processes previously believed to be "inherently sequential."** Examples include recurrent neural networks ([RNNs](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2407.19115)) and Markov chain Monte Carlo ([MCMC](https://alphaxiv.org/abs/2508.18413)). This ability to parallelize over the sequence length may seem like time travel or magic, but it is just an elegant application of Newton's method! I have proved under what conditions such parallelization techniques can yield dramatic speed-ups on GPUs over sequential evaluation, and developed scalable and stable parallelization techniques. I call these parallelization techniques *the [ungulates](https://colab.research.google.com/github/lindermanlab/hackathons/blob/master/notebooks/elk.ipynb)*---large hoofed mammals like [DEER](https://alphaxiv.org/abs/2309.12252) and [ELK](https://alphaxiv.org/abs/2407.19115). We are hard at work improving the ungulates and applying them to other domains! ------ Going forward, I am extremely interested in the quest to develop artificial general intelligence (AGI), and more broadly the study of intelligence---both natural and artificial. I am particularly interested in: - developing recurrent (transformer alternative) architectures that can more natively reason - developing hardware-aware AI algorithms, and novel hardware that can unlock novel AI algorithms - drawing inspiration from natural intelligence, and designing and scaling up neuro-inspired algorithms and hardware - applying AI to education technology to improve education and mentorship for the next generation **I'm actively looking for research jobs**, so please reach out if you know of a good fit! See my publications on my [Google Scholar page](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=5sj7cH8AAAAJ&hl=en). ::: {{< pagebreak >}} ::: {.column-page-inset .text-center} ```{=html} ``` :::
